issues.problem: “詹姆斯·威尔逊/James Wilson”中的名“詹姆斯/James”不见于证据。证据只称 Mr. Wilson。

evidence.quote: which Mr. Wilson read in the words following

issues.proposed: 改为“威尔逊/Mr. Wilson”。
issues.rationale: 中英文都删去名“詹姆斯/James”，改为“威尔逊/Mr. Wilson”，与证据称呼一致。

issues.problem: “不少人心知有缺点/Many in the room knew the document had flaws”写的是众人的内心认知。证据只记录了个别成员公开表示的异议。

evidence.quote: he too had objections
who may still have objections to it

issues.proposed: 改为“会上不少人公开表示过保留”/“Several members had voiced objections”。
issues.rationale: 删去“心知”这一内心状态描写，改为几位成员公开表示过异议，只陈述有记录的公开陈述。

issues.problem: “问题只剩一个：签不签，怎么签/One question was left”与证据不符。同日会议还通过了戈勒姆的修正案，并表决了会议记录的处置。

evidence.quote: might be yet reconsidered, in order to strike out "forty thousand," and insert "thirty thousand."
A question was then put on depositing the Journals

issues.proposed: 改为“最后的焦点是：签不签、怎么签”/“The central question was: sign it or not, and how.”
issues.rationale: “只剩一个”改为“摆在面前的一个问题”。同日还有戈勒姆修正案和会议记录处置，原写法不成立。

issues.problem: “到这里，争的已经不是文本好不好，而是手上有没有更好的东西可拿/By now the argument was not about...”是作者的概括，却写成了当日实况，没有标明是解释。
issues.proposed: 前加“作者认为”/“On one reading,”。
issues.rationale: 在概括句前加“作者认为/In the author's view”，标明这是作者的解释。

issues.problem: “于是当天真正的争点浮出水面/So the day's real dispute came into view”用因果连接，并断定何为“真正的争点”。这是作者的判断，未标为解释。
issues.proposed: 删“于是/So”，改为“作者认为，当天的一个核心争点是……”/“One reading is that a central dispute was...”。
issues.rationale: 删去因果连接“于是/So”，改为“作者认为，当天的一个核心争点是……”，不再断定何为“真正的”争点。

issues.problem: “他要的不是人人说好，而是名字出现在同一份文件上”（英文另有“one small thing”“Note the ask”）是对富兰克林意图的界定，未标为作者解释。证据只记录了他的请求本身。

evidence.quote: to make manifest our unanimity, put his name to this instrument

issues.proposed: 改为“一种解释是，他要的不是……”/“One reading: not that...”；删“one small thing”。
issues.rationale: 对富兰克林意图的界定前加“一种解释是/One reading”；英文删去“one small thing”和“Note the ask”。

issues.problem: 英文写了该条款“had produced so much discussion”，中文缺这一点。

evidence.quote: which had produced so much discussion

issues.proposed: 中文补“（该条款曾引起许多讨论）”。
issues.rationale: 中文补入“（该条款曾引起许多讨论）”，与英文对齐；英文不变。

issues.problem: 英文把麦迪逊的第三人称转述“He meant only to keep himself free...”放进引号，接在“he said”之后，读来像伦道夫的原话。

evidence.quote: He meant only to keep himself free to be governed by his duty, as it should be prescribed by his future judgment.

issues.proposed: 去掉引号改为转述，或写明“in Madison's words”。
issues.rationale: 英文去掉引号，改为间接转述，不再把麦迪逊的第三人称转述冒充伦道夫原话；中文本来就是转述，未改。

issues.problem: 汉密尔顿一句，英文有“might do infinite mischief”和“an enthusiasm…which might soon subside”，中文都缺。

evidence.quote: might do infinite mischief, by kindling the latent sparks that lurk under an enthusiasm in favor of the Convention which may soon subside

issues.proposed: 中文补“可能造成无穷祸害”“潜藏在可能很快消退的拥护热情之下的火星”。
issues.rationale: 中文补入“造成无穷祸害”和“潜藏在可能很快消退的拥护热情之下的火星”，与英文对齐。

issues.problem: 中英文都截去了“from the refusal of individuals to sign it”。原文的意思是：人们担心的无政府与内乱本来被归因于个别人拒签，伦道夫反指“全收或全拒”的方式才会导致这种结果。截断后这一对照丢失。

evidence.quote: would really produce the anarchy and civil convulsions which were apprehended from the refusal of individuals to sign it

issues.proposed: 补“（人们原以为个别人拒签才会招致的）”/“that were apprehended from the refusal of individuals to sign it”。
issues.rationale: 中英文都补回“人们原以为个别人拒签才会招致的/apprehended from the refusal of individuals to sign it”，恢复原文中的对照。

issues.problem: 中英不对称：中文缺“painful feelings”（痛苦心情）；英文缺两派相撞、混乱可忧一句。

evidence.quote: described the painful feelings of his situation
From the collision of these, in opposing and resisting the Constitution, confusion was greatly to be feared.

issues.proposed: 中文补“讲了自己处境的痛苦”；英文补“from the collision of the two, in resisting the Constitution, confusion was greatly to be feared”。
issues.rationale: 中文补“处境的痛苦”，并补全两派在反对宪法中相撞一层；英文补入两派相撞、混乱可忧一句。

issues.problem: 英文“Franklin's reply was light in tone but decisive”描述语气与效果，证据没有记载，中文也没有对应内容。
issues.proposed: 删去该描述，改为“Franklin replied:”。
issues.rationale: 英文删去无据的语气和效果描述，改为“Franklin replied:”；中文本无此内容，未改。

issues.problem: “那正是当天有人最想要的东西/wanted most”断言了程度。证据只显示有人希望人人签名、显示一致，并没有说这是他们“最想要”的。

evidence.quote: expressed his anxiety that every member should sign
to make manifest our unanimity

issues.proposed: 改为“而那正是当天有人力求的东西”/“the unanimity some in the room were pressing for”。
issues.rationale: “最想要/wanted most”改为“力求/pressing for”，不再断言程度。

issues.problem: 现代虚构场景直接引用了证据中富兰克林的原话，违反现代段不得引证据的规则。文中还称这句话“提供了”“记进纪要”的做法，但原句只讲意见留在墙内、从未外传。
issues.proposed: 删去引语和“、记进纪要”，改为不引史料的现代表述，如“会内把反对讲透，出了门不再外传”。
issues.rationale: 现代段删去富兰克林引语及“提供了”的说法，也删去“记进纪要”，改为不引史料的现代表述；ev 本来就为空。

issues.problem: “是一位与会者写下的记录/a participant's record”：证据没有说明麦迪逊是与会者。
issues.proposed: 删去该说法，或改为“麦迪逊的会议笔记”。
issues.rationale: 删去“是一位与会者写下的记录/a participant's record”。

issues.problem: 同F15，“一位与会者的记录/a participant's account”证据无据。

issues.problem: 中文“威尔逊反对销毁”言过其实，也与英文“prefers the second course”不一致。证据只说他倾向第二种办法，且曾一度更赞成销毁。

issues.proposed: 改为“威尔逊倾向交主席保管（他一度更赞成销毁）”。
issues.rationale: “反对销毁”改为“倾向交主席保管（他一度更赞成销毁）”；英文补“though he had at one time liked the first best”，中英对齐。

issues.problem: 中文“听候依宪法成立的国会处置”丢掉了原文的条件“if ever formed”，与英文不一致。

issues.rationale: 中文改为“听候日后若依宪法成立的国会处置”，恢复条件句。

issues.problem: “未替任何人补写动机或心理/no motive or psychology has been supplied”与正文不符：正文含有“不少人心知有缺点”（F2）、对富兰克林意图的界定（F6）、“light in tone but decisive”（F12）。

issues.rationale: 已按F2、F6、F12修正正文；uncertainty_note 保留不补写心理的保证，并补充说明作者的推断均已标明为解释。

issues.audit_rationale: “心知”是内心状态，证据只记录公开的异议。

issues.audit_rationale: 属于作者概括，却未标为解释。

issues.rationale: 同F15、F16，limits.0 和 uncertainty_note 中的“与会者”说法均已删去。

issues.audit_rationale: 威尔逊只是倾向保管，且曾一度更赞成销毁。

issues.rationale: 与M5相同。

issues.problem: [invented_inner_life] '到这里，争的已经不是文本好不好，而是手上有没有更好的东西可拿'——把作者对形势的推断写成当日实况
issues.rationale: 与M6相同。

issues.audit_rationale: 对富兰克林意图的正反界定未标为解释。
issues.rationale: 同F6，已标为“一种解释”。

issues.problem: 末句“会议室内的话，留在会议室内。/What was said in the chamber stayed in the chamber.”在 record 段里写成了陈述事实。证据只记载富兰克林说他本人的异议从未外传、将在这里消亡；它不能支持“会场内所说的话都没有外传”这一普遍结论，而且这句也没有标为解释。另外，“最硬的一段/The hardest passage”同样是未标注的评价。

evidence.quote: I have never whispered a syllable of them abroad. Within these walls they were born, and here they shall die.

issues.proposed: 末句改为归于富兰克林本人的立场，例如“他的意思是：他自己的异议留在会议室内。/His point: his own objections would stay in the chamber.”；“最硬的一段”改为中性表述，如“讲稿中有一段关于沉默”。
issues.rationale: I changed the evaluative opening "最硬的一段/The hardest passage" to the neutral "讲稿中有一段关于沉默/One passage of the speech is about silence". I rewrote the final sentence so it is attributed to Franklin's own position: "他的意思是：他自己的异议留在会议室内/His point: his own objections would stay in the chamber." The evidence only supports Franklin's statement that his own objections had not been spread outside the chamber. It does not support a general claim about everything said in the chamber.

issues.problem: 首句“记录本身的来路也值得留意/The record's own provenance deserves a look”紧接上段“记录主要来自麦迪逊的笔记”。这样写会让读者以为交主席保管的是本篇所依据的记录。证据中交主席保管的是会议官方的 Journals 及其他文件，与麦迪逊的笔记是两份不同的材料，正文把二者混为一谈。

evidence.quote: Mr. KING suggested that the Journals of the Convention should be either destroyed, or deposited in the custody of the president.

issues.proposed: 首句改为“会议官方日志（Journals，不同于麦迪逊的私人笔记）的去向也值得留意/The fate of the Convention's official Journals (distinct from Madison's notes) deserves a look”，后文“会议记录”统一改为“会议日志”。
issues.rationale: I rewrote the opening sentence to make clear that the papers handed to the presiding officer were the convention's official Journals and other papers. I also stated that these are a different body of material from the Madison notes this piece relies on. In the Chinese, "会议记录" is changed throughout to "会议日志". The English now consistently says Journals and makes clear that the discussion is recorded in Madison's notes for the same day.

issues.problem: 这一句放在富兰克林讲话之前：中文写“会上有几位成员公开表示过异议”，英文写“Several members openly voiced objections”。本段证据 F-E1 不支持这一点。证据包里当天公开表态的异议（伦道夫、格里等）都出现在讲话之后。F-E18 还记载，富兰克林写讲稿时并不知道会有哪位成员拒签。讲话时只能说仍有成员可能持有异议。

evidence.quote: every member of the Convention, who may still have objections to it
when drawing up that paper, he did not know that any particular member would refuse to sign his name to the instrument

issues.proposed: 改为“会要散了，会上仍可能有成员对这份文件持有异议。”英文改为“Some members might still have objections to the document on the table.”，并在本段 ev 中补上 F-E6。

issues.problem: 中文把“有意含糊”放在“麦迪逊记下一笔内情”之下，等于说这是麦迪逊的原话。麦迪逊原文只写“This ambiguous form”，并说明起草目的是争取异议者，没有写“有意”。英文版是“this ambiguous form”，与原文一致，因此中英不对等。

evidence.quote: This ambiguous form had been drawn up by Mr. Gouverneur Morris, in order to gain the dissenting members

issues.proposed: 中文改为“这个含糊的格式由古弗尼尔·莫里斯起草，为的是争取异议者……”

issues.problem: 中英文都说英文引语“均为麦迪逊笔记中的逐字片段”。但 sections.limits.0 引用的书名“Final Speech of Dr. Franklin in the late Federal Convention”出自1793年《富兰克林文集》，不是麦迪逊笔记。limits.0 自己已经限定为“正文的英文引语”，说明需要这个限定。

evidence.quote: Final Speech of Dr. Franklin in the late Federal Convention

issues.proposed: 中文改为“正文英文引语均为麦迪逊笔记中的逐字片段”，英文改为“All English quotations in the body are verbatim fragments of Madison's notes”。

edits.before: 1787年9月17日，制宪会议的最后一天。宪法的誊清本宣读完毕，本杰明·富兰克林站起身，手里拿着一份写好的讲稿；麦迪逊的笔记说，他是为了自己方便才把话写下来的，随后由詹姆斯·威尔逊代为宣读。会要散了，桌上这份文件不少人心知有缺点，问题只剩一个：签不签，怎么签。
edits.after: 1787年9月17日，制宪会议的最后一天。宪法的誊清本宣读完毕，本杰明·富兰克林站起身，手里拿着一份写好的讲稿；麦迪逊的笔记说，他是为了自己方便才把话写下来的，随后由威尔逊代为宣读。会要散了，对桌上这份文件，会上有几位成员公开表示过异议。摆在面前的一个问题是：签不签，怎么签。

edits.before: September 17, 1787, the last day of the Constitutional Convention. The engrossed Constitution had just been read aloud when Benjamin Franklin rose with a speech in his hand; Madison's notes say he had written it out for his own convenience, and James Wilson read it to the hall. The meeting was about to dissolve. Many in the room knew the document on the table had flaws. One question was left: sign it or not, and how.
edits.after: September 17, 1787, the last day of the Constitutional Convention. The engrossed Constitution had just been read aloud when Benjamin Franklin rose with a speech in his hand; Madison's notes say he had written it out for his own convenience, and Mr. Wilson read it to the hall. The meeting was about to dissolve. Several members openly voiced objections to the document on the table. One question before them: sign it or not, and how.

edits.before: Then came the request. To any member who still objected he asked one small thing: join him in a readiness to "doubt a little of his own infallibility", and put his name to the instrument, "to make manifest our unanimity". Note the ask — not that everyone praise the document, but that every name appear on the same page.

edits.before: Randolph rose and, alluding to Franklin's observations, apologized for refusing to sign, notwithstanding the vast majority and venerable names that would give the plan their sanction. Refusing, he said, did not mean he would oppose the Constitution outside the convention's doors: "He meant only to keep himself free to be governed by his duty, as it should be prescribed by his future judgment."

edits.before: 接着几位成员各自说明为什么签。莫里斯说，他也有异议，但视此为能得到的最好方案，愿连同缺点照收；多数已经决定，他服从这个决定；方案一出手，其余考虑都会退居其次，问题只剩“要不要有一个全国政府”，否则便是无政府。他并指出，按所提格式签名，只关乎出席各州一致这一事实。汉密尔顿说，他希望人人都签：几个有分量的人若反对甚至拒签，可能点燃潜藏的火星；在无政府与动荡、和方案可能带来的好处之间，没有什么可犹豫的。布朗特说，他本已声明不会以承诺支持的方式签名，但这个格式让他如释重负——他可以不承诺自己，只证明“方案是会议中各州一致的行动”这一事实。

edits.before: 富兰克林随即说明：写那篇讲稿时，他并不知道会有哪位成员拒签，希望大家这样理解；他感谢伦道夫最早提出方案、一路襄助，希望他放下异议，免得他的名字缺席带来大的祸害。伦道夫没有被说动。他说，以这个格式签名，与签宪法本身无异，换形式对他没有区别；拒签可能是他一生中最可怕的一步，但出于良知，他不能犹豫，更不能改变。他还说，把方案以“要么全收、要么全拒”的最终选择交给民众，会真的带来人们担心的无政府和内乱。
edits.after: 富兰克林随即说明：写那篇讲稿时，他并不知道会有哪位成员拒签，希望大家这样理解；他感谢伦道夫最早提出方案、一路襄助，希望他放下异议，免得他的名字缺席带来大的祸害。伦道夫没有被说动。他说，以这个格式签名，与签宪法本身无异，换形式对他没有区别；拒签可能是他一生中最可怕的一步，但出于良知，他不能犹豫，更不能改变。他还说，把方案以“要么全收、要么全拒”的最终选择交给民众，真正会带来的，正是人们原以为个别人拒签才会招致的无政府和内乱。

edits.before: Franklin explained that when drawing up that paper he had not known that any particular member would refuse to sign, and hoped to be so understood. He felt a high sense of obligation to Randolph for bringing the plan forward in the first instance and for his help along the way, and hoped he would yet lay aside his objections and prevent the great mischief that the refusal of his name might produce. Randolph was not moved. To sign in the proposed form was, for him, the same as signing the Constitution; the change of form made no difference. Refusing might be the most awful step of his life, but conscience dictated it, and he could not hesitate, much less change. He added that holding out the plan to the people with a final alternative of accepting or rejecting it in toto would really produce the anarchy and civil convulsions that were apprehended.

Randolph was not moved. To sign in the proposed form was, for him, the same as signing the Constitution; the change of form made no difference. Refusing might be the most awful step of his life, but conscience dictated it, and he could not hesitate, much less change. He added that holding out the plan to the people with a final alternative of accepting or rejecting it in toto would really produce the very anarchy and civil convulsions that were apprehended from the refusal of individuals to sign it.

edits.before: 格里接着讲了自己的处境：他担心眼前的局面会引发内战，尤其在马萨诸塞，那里一派倾向民主——他认为那是最坏的政治祸害——另一派走向相反的极端，两派相撞，混乱可忧。格式对他同样无关紧要。但他说，如果别处不会让人知道，拒签的事绝不会由他传出去；他又说，富兰克林的话他只能看作是针对他和其他不签名的人。

edits.before: Gerry then described the painful feelings of his situation and his fear that the present crisis might end in civil war — in Massachusetts especially, where one party was devoted to democracy, which he thought the worst of all political evils, and the other as violent at the opposite extreme. The form meant nothing to him either. But if it were not otherwise apparent, the refusals to sign should never be known from him. As for Franklin's remarks, he said, he could only view them as levelled at himself and the other gentlemen who meant not to sign.
edits.after: Gerry then described the painful feelings of his situation and his fear that the present crisis might end in civil war — in Massachusetts especially, where one party was devoted to democracy, which he thought the worst of all political evils, and the other as violent at the opposite extreme; from the collision of the two, in opposing and resisting the Constitution, confusion was greatly to be feared. The form meant nothing to him either. But if it were not otherwise apparent, the refusals to sign should never be known from him. As for Franklin's remarks, he said, he could only view them as levelled at himself and the other gentlemen who meant not to sign.

edits.before: Others found the form too coy. Pinckney thought ambiguity would win few converts; better to be candid and let the form speak the substance. He meant to sign with a view to supporting the Constitution with all his influence, and would pledge himself accordingly. Franklin's reply was light in tone but decisive: "It is too soon to pledge ourselves, before Congress and our constituents shall have approved the plan." Ingersoll offered another reading: the signature was neither a bare attestation of the fact nor a pledge to support the plan at all events, but "a recommendation of what, all things considered, was the most eligible".

edits.before: 另一种解释针对富兰克林请大家“稍稍怀疑一下自己的不会出错”的那句话。作者的引申是：这句话提供的也许不是“方案是对的”这种理由，而是一种在不确定中签字的态度——当另开一次会未必更好时，先承认自己可能错，再把名字放上去。作者提出的替代选择是要求在签名旁写明保留意见；但作者同样承认，那样做会削弱“一致”的分量，而那正是当天有人最想要的东西。

edits.before: A second reading turns on Franklin's plea to "doubt a little of his own infallibility". The author's extension, not Franklin's words: what he offered may have been less a reason to call the plan right than a posture for signing under uncertainty. When another convention might well do no better, first admit you may be wrong, then put your name down. The author's alternative would be to require a written reservation beside each signature, but the author also grants that this would weaken the unanimity that some in the room wanted most that day.

edits.before: Fictional modern scene one. A review committee has just turned down a plan that one colleague pushed hard for. Afterwards a member tells someone in the corridor that they had disagreed too and were simply outvoted. Franklin's line, "Within these walls they were born, and here they shall die," points to another way: argue the objection fully in the room and get it into the minutes, then stop treating a settled disagreement as gossip once you are outside. That is not hiding the outcome; it is declining to fight the same battle again in the hallway.

edits.before: 这场会议的记录主要来自詹姆斯·麦迪逊的笔记，后收入1845年埃利奥特编本（维基文库），是一位与会者写下的记录。1793年出版的《富兰克林文集》收有这篇讲稿的印本（题作 Final Speech of Dr. Franklin in the late Federal Convention），可以拿来对照，但本篇没有逐字比对两版。正文的英文引语都取自麦迪逊笔记一版；富兰克林讲稿的措辞在两版间是否有出入，本篇不作断言。

edits.before: 记录本身的来路也值得留意。同日的笔记里，金建议销毁会议记录或交主席保管，理由是记录若公开，会被想阻挠宪法的人利用；威尔逊反对销毁，说虚假说法可能流传，不应让反驳无从谈起；最终决定把记录交主席保管，听候依宪法成立的国会处置。至于富兰克林关于太阳的那段话，笔记记的是他望着椅背，对身边几位成员说的——那是对身边几个人说的话，不是对全场的正式演说。另外，本篇只写到1787年9月17日会议散会为止，不涉及宪法此后的批准与修正。

In these notes King suggests that the journals be destroyed or left in the president's custody, since made public they would be put to bad use by those wishing to prevent the Constitution's adoption; Wilson prefers the second course — false suggestions may be spread, and it should not be made impossible to contradict them — and the papers are left with the president, subject to the order of Congress, if ever formed under the Constitution. In any case, this piece stops at the adjournment of 17 September 1787 and touches neither ratification nor amendment.

edits.before: The record comes chiefly from Madison's notes (Elliot's 1845 edition, Wikisource), a participant's account; the speech as printed in the 1793 Works of Franklin can serve as a check, and the two have not been collated word by word here. All English quotations are verbatim fragments of Madison's notes; speeches are reported as the notes give them, and no motive or psychology has been supplied for anyone.
edits.after: The record comes chiefly from Madison's notes (Elliot's 1845 edition, Wikisource); the speech as printed in the 1793 Works of Franklin can serve as a check, and the two have not been collated word by word here. All English quotations are verbatim fragments of Madison's notes; speeches are reported as the notes give them, no motive or psychology has been supplied for anyone, and the author's inferences are marked as interpretation.

edits.before: 讲稿里最硬的一段是关于沉默的。富兰克林说，他对宪法缺点的意见，已为公共利益而放弃，从未在外面透露一个字：“它们在这几面墙里产生，也将在这里消亡。”会议室内的话，留在会议室内。
edits.after: 讲稿中有一段关于沉默。富兰克林说，他对宪法缺点的意见，已为公共利益而放弃，从未在外面透露一个字：“它们在这几面墙里产生，也将在这里消亡。”他的意思是：他自己的异议留在会议室内。

edits.before: The hardest passage of the speech is about silence. Franklin said the opinions he had held of the Constitution's errors he sacrificed to the public good, and had never whispered a syllable of them abroad: "Within these walls they were born, and here they shall die." What was said in the chamber stayed in the chamber.
edits.after: One passage of the speech is about silence. Franklin said the opinions he had held of the Constitution's errors he sacrificed to the public good, and had never whispered a syllable of them abroad: "Within these walls they were born, and here they shall die." His point: his own objections would stay in the chamber.

edits.before: 记录本身的来路也值得留意。同日的笔记里，金建议销毁会议记录或交主席保管，理由是记录若公开，会被想阻挠宪法的人利用；威尔逊倾向交主席保管（他一度更赞成销毁），说虚假说法可能流传，不应让反驳无从谈起；最终决定把记录交主席保管，听候日后若依宪法成立的国会处置。至于富兰克林关于太阳的那段话，笔记记的是他望着椅背，对身边几位成员说的——那是对身边几个人说的话，不是对全场的正式演说。另外，本篇只写到1787年9月17日会议散会为止，不涉及宪法此后的批准与修正。
edits.after: 会议官方日志及其他文件的去向也值得留意，它们和本篇所依据的麦迪逊笔记是两份不同的材料。同日的笔记里，金建议销毁会议日志或交主席保管，理由是日志若公开，会被想阻挠宪法的人利用；威尔逊倾向交主席保管（他一度更赞成销毁），说虚假说法可能流传，不应让反驳无从谈起；最终决定把日志及其他文件交主席保管，听候日后若依宪法成立的国会处置。至于富兰克林关于太阳的那段话，笔记记的是他望着椅背，对身边几位成员说的——那是对身边几个人说的话，不是对全场的正式演说。另外，本篇只写到1787年9月17日会议散会为止，不涉及宪法此后的批准与修正。

edits.before: The record's own provenance deserves a look. In these notes King suggests that the journals be destroyed or left in the president's custody, since made public they would be put to bad use by those wishing to prevent the Constitution's adoption; Wilson prefers the second course, though he had at one time liked the first best — false suggestions may be spread, and it should not be made impossible to contradict them — and the papers are left with the president, subject to the order of Congress, if ever formed under the Constitution. As for Franklin and the sun, the notes record that he observed to a few members near him: an aside to those beside him, not a formal address to the whole hall. In any case, this piece stops at the adjournment of 17 September 1787 and touches neither ratification nor amendment.
edits.after: The fate of the Convention's official Journals and other papers also deserves a look; they are a different set of papers from the Madison notes this piece relies on. In Madison's notes for the same day, King suggests that the Journals be destroyed or left in the president's custody, since made public they would be put to bad use by those wishing to prevent the Constitution's adoption; Wilson prefers the second course, though he had at one time liked the first best — false suggestions may be spread, and it should not be made impossible to contradict them — and the Journals and other papers are left with the president, subject to the order of Congress, if ever formed under the Constitution. As for Franklin and the sun, the notes record that he observed to a few members near him: an aside to those beside him, not a formal address to the whole hall. In any case, this piece stops at the adjournment of 17 September 1787 and touches neither ratification nor amendment.

issues.problem: 末句“会议室内的话，留在会议室内。/What was said in the chamber stayed in the chamber.”在 record 段里写成了陈述事实。证据只记载富兰克林说他本人的异议从未外传、将在这里消亡；它不能支持“会场内所说的话都没有外传”这一普遍结论，而且这句也没有标为解释。另外，“最硬的一段/The hardest passage”同样是未标注的评价。

evidence.quote: I have never whispered a syllable of them abroad. Within these walls they were born, and here they shall die.

issues.proposed: 末句改为归于富兰克林本人的立场，例如“他的意思是：他自己的异议留在会议室内。/His point: his own objections would stay in the chamber.”；“最硬的一段”改为中性表述，如“讲稿中有一段关于沉默”。

issues.problem: 首句“记录本身的来路也值得留意/The record's own provenance deserves a look”紧接上段“记录主要来自麦迪逊的笔记”。这样写会让读者以为交主席保管的是本篇所依据的记录。证据中交主席保管的是会议官方的 Journals 及其他文件，与麦迪逊的笔记是两份不同的材料，正文把二者混为一谈。

evidence.quote: Mr. KING suggested that the Journals of the Convention should be either destroyed, or deposited in the custody of the president.

issues.proposed: 首句改为“会议官方日志（Journals，不同于麦迪逊的私人笔记）的去向也值得留意/The fate of the Convention's official Journals (distinct from Madison's notes) deserves a look”，后文“会议记录”统一改为“会议日志”。

verify.overall: 定稿整体有证据支撑：引语逐字准确，推断均已标注，中英文一致。需修改两处：story.0 末句未标注的泛化陈述，以及 limits.1 把会议官方日志与麦迪逊笔记混为一谈。

issues.problem: 这一句放在富兰克林讲话之前：中文写“会上有几位成员公开表示过异议”，英文写“Several members openly voiced objections”。本段证据 F-E1 不支持这一点。证据包里当天公开表态的异议（伦道夫、格里等）都出现在讲话之后。F-E18 还记载，富兰克林写讲稿时并不知道会有哪位成员拒签。讲话时只能说仍有成员可能持有异议。

evidence.quote: every member of the Convention, who may still have objections to it
when drawing up that paper, he did not know that any particular member would refuse to sign his name to the instrument

issues.proposed: 改为“会要散了，会上仍可能有成员对这份文件持有异议。”英文改为“Some members might still have objections to the document on the table.”，并在本段 ev 中补上 F-E6。

issues.problem: 中文把“有意含糊”放在“麦迪逊记下一笔内情”之下，等于说这是麦迪逊的原话。麦迪逊原文只写“This ambiguous form”，并说明起草目的是争取异议者，没有写“有意”。英文版是“this ambiguous form”，与原文一致，因此中英不对等。

evidence.quote: This ambiguous form had been drawn up by Mr. Gouverneur Morris, in order to gain the dissenting members

issues.proposed: 中文改为“这个含糊的格式由古弗尼尔·莫里斯起草，为的是争取异议者……”

issues.problem: 中英文都说英文引语“均为麦迪逊笔记中的逐字片段”。但 sections.limits.0 引用的书名“Final Speech of Dr. Franklin in the late Federal Convention”出自1793年《富兰克林文集》，不是麦迪逊笔记。limits.0 自己已经限定为“正文的英文引语”，说明需要这个限定。

evidence.quote: Final Speech of Dr. Franklin in the late Federal Convention

issues.proposed: 中文改为“正文英文引语均为麦迪逊笔记中的逐字片段”，英文改为“All English quotations in the body are verbatim fragments of Madison's notes”。

verify.overall: 定稿整体有证据支撑，引语逐字准确，解释性内容均已标注。需小修三处：hook.0 的时间顺序、story.2 中文“有意含糊”的归属，以及 uncertainty_note 对引语来源的表述范围。

issues.problem: “詹姆斯·威尔逊/James Wilson”中的名“詹姆斯/James”不见于证据。证据只称 Mr. Wilson。

evidence.quote: which Mr. Wilson read in the words following

issues.proposed: 改为“威尔逊/Mr. Wilson”。

issues.problem: “不少人心知有缺点/Many in the room knew the document had flaws”写的是众人的内心认知。证据只记录了个别成员公开表示的异议。

evidence.quote: he too had objections
who may still have objections to it

issues.proposed: 改为“会上不少人公开表示过保留”/“Several members had voiced objections”。

issues.problem: “问题只剩一个：签不签，怎么签/One question was left”与证据不符。同日会议还通过了戈勒姆的修正案，并表决了会议记录的处置。

evidence.quote: might be yet reconsidered, in order to strike out "forty thousand," and insert "thirty thousand."
A question was then put on depositing the Journals

issues.proposed: 改为“最后的焦点是：签不签、怎么签”/“The central question was: sign it or not, and how.”

issues.problem: “到这里，争的已经不是文本好不好，而是手上有没有更好的东西可拿/By now the argument was not about...”是作者的概括，却写成了当日实况，没有标明是解释。
issues.proposed: 前加“作者认为”/“On one reading,”。

issues.problem: “于是当天真正的争点浮出水面/So the day's real dispute came into view”用因果连接，并断定何为“真正的争点”。这是作者的判断，未标为解释。
issues.proposed: 删“于是/So”，改为“作者认为，当天的一个核心争点是……”/“One reading is that a central dispute was...”。

issues.problem: “他要的不是人人说好，而是名字出现在同一份文件上”（英文另有“one small thing”“Note the ask”）是对富兰克林意图的界定，未标为作者解释。证据只记录了他的请求本身。

evidence.quote: to make manifest our unanimity, put his name to this instrument

issues.proposed: 改为“一种解释是，他要的不是……”/“One reading: not that...”；删“one small thing”。

issues.problem: 英文写了该条款“had produced so much discussion”，中文缺这一点。

evidence.quote: which had produced so much discussion

issues.proposed: 中文补“（该条款曾引起许多讨论）”。

issues.problem: 英文把麦迪逊的第三人称转述“He meant only to keep himself free...”放进引号，接在“he said”之后，读来像伦道夫的原话。

evidence.quote: He meant only to keep himself free to be governed by his duty, as it should be prescribed by his future judgment.

issues.proposed: 去掉引号改为转述，或写明“in Madison's words”。

issues.problem: 汉密尔顿一句，英文有“might do infinite mischief”和“an enthusiasm…which might soon subside”，中文都缺。

evidence.quote: might do infinite mischief, by kindling the latent sparks that lurk under an enthusiasm in favor of the Convention which may soon subside

issues.proposed: 中文补“可能造成无穷祸害”“潜藏在可能很快消退的拥护热情之下的火星”。

issues.problem: 中英文都截去了“from the refusal of individuals to sign it”。原文的意思是：人们担心的无政府与内乱本来被归因于个别人拒签，伦道夫反指“全收或全拒”的方式才会导致这种结果。截断后这一对照丢失。

evidence.quote: would really produce the anarchy and civil convulsions which were apprehended from the refusal of individuals to sign it

issues.proposed: 补“（人们原以为个别人拒签才会招致的）”/“that were apprehended from the refusal of individuals to sign it”。

issues.problem: 中英不对称：中文缺“painful feelings”（痛苦心情）；英文缺两派相撞、混乱可忧一句。

evidence.quote: described the painful feelings of his situation
From the collision of these, in opposing and resisting the Constitution, confusion was greatly to be feared.

issues.proposed: 中文补“讲了自己处境的痛苦”；英文补“from the collision of the two, in resisting the Constitution, confusion was greatly to be feared”。

issues.problem: 英文“Franklin's reply was light in tone but decisive”描述语气与效果，证据没有记载，中文也没有对应内容。
issues.proposed: 删去该描述，改为“Franklin replied:”。

issues.problem: “那正是当天有人最想要的东西/wanted most”断言了程度。证据只显示有人希望人人签名、显示一致，并没有说这是他们“最想要”的。

evidence.quote: expressed his anxiety that every member should sign
to make manifest our unanimity

issues.proposed: 改为“而那正是当天有人力求的东西”/“the unanimity some in the room were pressing for”。

issues.problem: 现代虚构场景直接引用了证据中富兰克林的原话，违反现代段不得引证据的规则。文中还称这句话“提供了”“记进纪要”的做法，但原句只讲意见留在墙内、从未外传。
issues.proposed: 删去引语和“、记进纪要”，改为不引史料的现代表述，如“会内把反对讲透，出了门不再外传”。

issues.problem: “是一位与会者写下的记录/a participant's record”：证据没有说明麦迪逊是与会者。
issues.proposed: 删去该说法，或改为“麦迪逊的会议笔记”。

issues.problem: 同F15，“一位与会者的记录/a participant's account”证据无据。
issues.proposed: 删去“一位与会者的记录/a participant's account”。
